Implementer note (not evidence). Review of spec `pose-generation-bound-query-cursors` (B36): MCP list pagination moves from a version 1 offset cursor to a signed, versioned token bound to tool, project, filters and the ordered collection with its index generation; a changed collection, another query, an expired token, a version 1 token or a server restart is refused with a `cursor-*` code and the caller restarts from the first page; pages are bounded to 500 items and disclose generation, collection and total; calls without cursor and limit are unchanged. The ADR `generation-bound-query-cursors` records the design and the rejected alternatives; no index-backed limit was introduced because none of the five list collections is indexed (open follow-up). The spec already carries its Validation, requirement trace and Final Report. Do NOT run `pose validate`, `pose index`, `pose assess ...` or any command that writes to the repository. Targeted `go test` may fail on a read-only sandbox; then rely on the sealed evidence. Report every defect at once, classified blocker or follow-up.

Evidence references: the engine refuses a conclusion whose criterion cites a structural fact (an `SD-...` id), a requirement id (`R<N>`) or a file path as its evidence. Cite the bundle's `structure:design-<id>` evidence for design-causality and assumption-integrity, and sealed `unit:`, `integration:`, `build:` or `e2e:` ids for the others. Check each plan tool's `evidence_classes` and cite every class it lists; for `surface-check` that means one sealed `integration:` and one sealed `reachability:` evidence id (for example `reachability:pose-mcp/go/delivery-reachability` and `integration:pose-mcp/go/delivery-integration`) besides the result of running the tool.

Round 2 of this review: the previous pass raised seven findings (generation read after the collection, incomplete spec result keys, token size on issue, unbounded continuation without limit, undisclosed full-scan cost, non-canonical filters, spec artifact declared as created); each was corrected and covered by a test named in the spec's requirement trace. Verify the corrections and look for new defects.

Round 3 of this review: the previous pass raised three findings (explicit non-positive or null limits on four tools, the index reader's Diverged/Reason discarded, non-canonical since); the first two were corrected and covered by tests in the requirement trace, since is now normalized, and the default-sort canonicalization is an open follow-up. Verify the corrections and look for new defects.

Round 4 of this review: the previous pass asked for R8 measurements (now `TestPageCostIsMeasuredAndBounded`, logged numbers in the spec's Known gaps, indexed case dispositioned as the open follow-up) and for an end-to-end test of the index reader's Diverged/Reason propagation (now `TestAPageCarriesTheIndexReadersStatusReasonAndDivergedFiles`). The default-sort canonicalization stays an owned follow-up. Verify and look for new defects; classify anything you consider a blocker against the requirements, not against hypothetical features.

Round 5 of this review: the previous pass raised two blockers (a differently-cased `Limit` alias bypassing the limit check, and every page re-hashing all index files) and one owned follow-up. Both blockers were corrected: aliases of limit and cursor are refused (`TestAnAliasOfLimitOrCursorIsRefused`), and the generation verification is reused while its files are unchanged (`TestAPageDoesNotReverifyAnUnchangedGeneration`: 14.7 MB on the first call, 31 KB on the next page). Verify and look for new defects; classify a finding as a blocker only if a stated requirement is violated.

Round 6 of this review: the previous pass raised two blockers (a `Cursor` alias on pose_list_specs restarting a walk, and the generation cache ignoring symlink targets) and the default-sort follow-up. All three were corrected: pose_list_specs now runs the same alias and limit validation (`TestACursorAliasCannotRestartAWalk`), the cache signature follows link targets and their metadata (`TestAReusedGenerationSeesASymlinkTargetChange`), and an omitted sort is canonicalized to `slug` (`TestAnOmittedSortAndSlugSortAreTheSameQuery`, which also proves the default order is slug order). Verify and look for new defects; a blocker is a violated stated requirement.

Round 7 of this review: the previous pass raised three blockers, all corrected with tests named in the requirement trace: a null `cursor` is refused on every paginated tool (`TestANullCursorIsRefusedOnEveryPaginatedTool`); the filter tuple is JSON-encoded so distinct queries cannot serialize alike (`TestFiltersThatSerializeAlikeBindDifferentCursors`); the generation cache signature adds the inode and status-change time on Linux, so an edit that restores size and mtime is seen (`TestAReusedGenerationSeesAnEditThatPreservesSizeAndModTime`). Verify and look for new defects; a blocker is a violated stated requirement, and an accepted limit already written in the ADR is not a finding.
